posts.text:
Introducing Claude Haiku 5.5: the cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model we’ve ever released.

On average, it costs around 75% less to run than Claude Haiku 4.5.
posts.why_viral: Official launch of a major cost-reduced capable small model with strong benchmarks and pricing transparency.
posts.why_it_matters: Gives builders a cheaper high-volume model for agents, coding subtasks, and production workloads with adjustable effort.

posts.text:
We’re releasing a broad range of new mathematical results produced by an internal frontier model.

We’ve been consulting with the independent Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence at the Institute for Advanced Study, and we have drawn on their advice and public recommendations to inform how we release these results.
posts.why_viral: OpenAI releasing frontier-model-generated math results with independent advisory input.
posts.why_it_matters: Signals progress on hard reasoning and provides new open mathematical results developers can study or build on.

posts.text:
GPT-6 and Intelligent UI, now rolling out in ChatGPT for everyone.

Intelligent UI in ChatGPT delivers fast, interactive answers that make everyday questions more visual, complex topics easier to grasp, and interactive tools for your task available on the spot.
posts.why_viral: Broad rollout of GPT-6 with interactive visual UI across ChatGPT tiers.
posts.why_it_matters: Changes how users interact with the model; interactive charts, tools, and visuals become available in the main ChatGPT experience.

posts.text:
Claude Managed Agents dynamic workflows are now available in public beta. It's a new type of multiagent orchestration, built for your most ambitious workloads.

A lead agent writes a plan that runs across many agents in phases, combining the results at the end.
posts.why_viral: Public beta of multi-agent orchestration for complex workflows.
posts.why_it_matters: Enables developers to build phased multi-agent systems with a lead planner more easily on Claude.

posts.text:
Meet Nano Banana 2.1, our latest image generation and editing model 🍌

This upgraded version outperforms our previous models across the board, with notable leaps in visual design, mask-based editing, and subject consistency to help you create more natural-looking images.
posts.why_viral: Official upgrade to Google’s image generation model with stronger editing capabilities.
posts.why_it_matters: Improves on-device and product image gen/editing consistency for apps and design tools.

posts.text:
Let your app choose the right model, tool, or action in near real-time with Decisions API, now available to all developers in public beta.

The Decisions API makes decisions up to 10x faster than GPT-6 Luna through the Responses API.
posts.why_viral: New API for fast routing/classification/scoring decisions.
posts.why_it_matters: Lets developers build cheaper, faster model/tool routers and evaluators without full generation calls.

posts.text:
We’re beginning a process of publishing more frequent reports on model behavior, beyond what appears in our system cards and regular risk reports.

Today’s report describes four types of behaviors we’ve identified during evaluations and internal use. In each, Claude acted on real websites or systems in ways we didn’t intend, sometimes by working around a restriction instead of stopping.

All cases had minimal real-world impact. From an alignment and security perspective, we consider these behaviors significantly less severe than the cybersecurity incidents we reported in July and September.

Read the full report:
posts.why_viral: Transparent reporting of unintended model behaviors in real systems.
posts.why_it_matters: Gives developers concrete examples of alignment edge cases to watch when deploying agents with tool access.

posts.text:
We’re releasing EmbeddingGemma 2, our first natively multimodal open model engineered for on-device embeddings.

Built on the Gemma 4 architecture and released under an Apache 2.0 license, it goes beyond text to unify images, video, audio, and code in a single embedding space.
posts.why_viral: Open multimodal embedding model for on-device use.
posts.why_it_matters: Enables local multimodal retrieval and RAG without sending data to the cloud.

How to build automations with Claude Managed Agents: https://claude.dev/blog/building-effective-agent-automations/

Deploy an agent that reads Slack/GitHub on a schedule (with credentials and memory) and posts updates. You can set it up with a Claude Code command and use the new API credits included in Max and Team.

posts.text:
After @elonmusk tweeted my guide to connecting Claude and ChatGPT to Grok @Bot, people had 5 questions.

1. Do I need an API key?
Nah. Just log into Claude or ChatGPT, like you do in VS Code, terminal, etc.

2. Do I need new subscriptions?
Nope. Just use the Claude and ChatGPT plans you already pay for. Now you get more for your $

3. What's the point?
Claude writes closer to my taste. And some projects only come out right on certain models.

4. Won't Claude or ChatGPT log me out when Grok logs in?
I never got logged out. My Grok @Bot & my Mac both access those subscrptions.

5. How do I set it up?
Easy! Just send your Grok Bot this:

"Connect to my Claude and ChatGPT subscriptions using Claude Code and Codex."

It opens a terminal on its computer, installs both command-line tools, and asks you to log in. That's it.
posts.why_viral: Practical Q&A resolving setup friction for multi-model agent access.
posts.why_it_matters: Shows founders and developers how to route work across Claude, ChatGPT, and Grok without extra keys or logouts.

posts.text:
I'm sharing with you one of the best papers I've read on Harness Engineering

it takes apart Claude Code (Opus 5.5), Codex, Gemini CLI and more, and boils all of them down to one line:

agent = model + harness

what you walk away with:
> what a harness actually is
> how today's coding agents are built under the hood
> the patterns every one of them repeats
> where the whole category is heading
> their checklist for building your own

the model gets the headlines. the harness decides whether the agent works

loop and graph engineering on top of it - in my article below
posts.why_viral: Distills coding-agent architecture into a clear harness model with a checklist.
posts.why_it_matters: Helps builders understand why the harness (loops, tools, memory, verification) matters more than the base model for reliable agents.

posts.text:
Excellent agentic coding interview. 

Key points:

Build a “trust ladder”. The more you can constrain the agent’s output, the more you can trust it. 

Instead of a mere “software factory”, try to create a “Michelin restaurant”. Create processes and tools that make beautiful code automatically.

Think about code reviews like sampling. You can’t afford to taste every dish, but you should spot check.

Ask “where am I the bottleneck? How can I get the agent to answer its own questions?”

Create inner loops and outer loops. Inner loops accomplish tasks. Outer loops coordinate inner loops and analyze the big picture.

Your skills should get smaller over time as agents improve.. Focus on workflows, not implementation details. 

Connectors trigger new work. Connect your bots to Jira, GitHub issues, etc so they begin work automatically.

Make it easy for agents to verify their work. Create a CLI for your app and a skill that calls the CLI. Then agents can verify their work consistently and efficiently.

A good code base is easy to change.
posts.why_viral: Sharp, practical lessons from an agentic coding interview on trust, loops, and verification.
posts.why_it_matters: Gives founders and developers concrete patterns for making coding agents more reliable and less bottlenecked.
